verification_note: PARTIALLY verified. On 2026-11-03 the official page https://www.psacard.com/gradingstandards was read through an automated fetch that returns a summary of the page; the items listed under official_items match that reading. The page has no grade-by-grade table, so every other numeric value (PSA 9 reverse limit, centering for grades 8 and below, the 'one minor flaw' wording for PSA 9) still comes from secondary sources. Compare against the page yourself before relying on any value.
centering_measure: Larger border share on the worse axis, in percent (60 means 60/40).
leeway_note: Secondary sources report that PSA allows a 5 percent leeway on front centering for cards grading 7 or better, and may permit a small variance based on overall eye appeal. GradeForge uses the leeway only for its optimistic ceiling, never for the conservative one.
known_conflicts: The official page gives the PSA 10 front limit as a range, 'approximately 55/45 to 60/40'. Secondary sources usually say 55/45. GradeForge treats 55/45 as the nominal limit and 55-60 as a grader-discretion band.
Some sources call 60/40 the PSA 10 front limit (older guidance). Under the official wording it is the outer end of the discretion band, not a safe pass.
Isolated sources list different values for PSA 6, 7 and 8 (for example 75/25, 80/20, 95/5). The values below are the ones most sources agree on.

10.name: Gem Mint
10.summary: Virtually perfect card: four sharp corners, sharp focus, full original gloss, no staining.

9.name: Mint
9.summary: Superb card that tolerates one minor flaw, such as a slight wax stain on the back, a minor print imperfection, or slightly off-white borders.

8.name: Near Mint-Mint
8.summary: Looks like a 9 at first glance; may show slight fraying at one or two corners, a minor print flaw, or slight staining.

7.name: Near Mint
7.summary: Slight surface wear and slight corner fraying visible.

6.name: Excellent-Mint
6.summary: Visible surface wear or a print defect that does not detract from overall appeal.

5.name: Excellent
5.summary: Minor corner rounding is evident; surface wear and print defects are more visible; borders may look off-white.

4.name: Very Good-Excellent
4.summary: Slightly rounded corners; surface wear is noticeable but modest.

3.name: Very Good
3.summary: Corner rounding is evident but not extreme; wear is apparent, possibly with light scuffing or scratches.

2.name: Good
2.summary: Accelerated corner rounding; surface wear is obvious.

1.name: Poor
1.summary: Card is complete but heavily worn.

not_modeled_note: GradeForge does not predict qualifiers (it records them as feedback) and does not model PSA's authentication or alteration checks.

official_items.text: A PSA 10 card is a virtually perfect card. Attributes include four perfectly sharp corners, sharp focus and full original gloss.
A PSA 10 card must be free of staining of any kind. A slight printing imperfection is allowed only if it does not impair the overall appeal of the card.
Image centered within a tolerance not to exceed approximately 55/45 to 60/40 percent on the front.
A card meeting all other PSA 9 requirements that measures 60/40 on the front automatically meets the PSA 9 front centering standard; it may be deemed to meet it at 65/35 if eye appeal is good.
A 5% leeway is given to the front centering minimum standards for cards which grade PSA 7 or better.
Graders reserve the right, based on the strength or weakness of eye appeal, to make a judgment call on the grade.
Off-center cards are designated OC or receive a numeric grade reflecting the minimum centering allowed.
